Sirmilik is an area rich in wildlife that has sustained Inuit for thousands of years. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/nu/sirmilik/WET4/index/hoodoos-640x360.jpg?modified=20240104182118)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/sirmilik/activ/randonnees-hiking) ### [Explore glaciers and hoodoos](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/sirmilik/activ/randonnees-hiking) Hike or ski through the diverse terrain of Bylot Island and the Borden Peninsula. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/nu/sirmilik/WET4/activ/narval-narwhal-640x360.jpg?modified=20240104181535)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/sirmilik/activ/faune-wildlife) ### [Floe edge safari](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/sirmilik/activ/faune-wildlife) See polar bears, whales, seals and birds where ice meets open water. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/nu/sirmilik/WET4/index/ours-bears-640x360.jpg?modified=20240104195818)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/sirmilik/info) ### [Cooperative management](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/sirmilik/info) Learn how Inuit and Parks Canada work together to manage Sirmilik National Park. ## Most requested - Park office: [Complete schedule](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/sirmilik/visit/heures-hours) ### \#SirmilikNP - [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/ParksCanadaNunavut/) - [Twitter](https://x.com/ParksCanNunavut) ## More places to discover with Parks Canada [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/nu/auyuittuq-640x360.jpg?modified=20221126220409)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/auyuittuq) ### [Auyuittuq National Park](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/auyuittuq) Home to spectacular natural landmarks like the Akshayuk Pass, Thor Peak and the Penny Ice Cap, Auyuittuq is the “land that never melts” in Inuktitut. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/nu/qausuittuq-640x360.jpg?modified=20221126220409)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/qausuittuq) ### [Qausuittuq National Park](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/qausuittuq) A home for the endangered Peary caribou and a traditional Inuit hunting and fishing area on Bathurst Island in Nunavut’s High Arctic. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/nu/quttinirpaaq-640x360.jpg?modified=20221126220410)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/quttinirpaaq) ### [Quttinirpaaq National Park](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/quttinirpaaq) Inuktitut for “land at the top of the world”, Quttinirpaaq is Canada’s northernmost national park, a vast arctic wilderness on Ellesmere Island. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/nu/ukkusiksalik-640x360.jpg?modified=20221126220410)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/ukkusiksalik) ### [Ukkusiksalik National Park](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/ukkusiksalik) An area rich in arctic wildlife and Inuit history where hundreds of archaeological sites dot the landscape surrounding Wager Bay. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/nu/epaves-wrecks-640x360.jpg?modified=20221126220409)](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/nu/epaveswrecks) ### [Wrecks of HMS Erebus and HMS Terror National Historic Site](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/nu/epaveswrecks) Learn about Sir John Franklin’s legendary 1845 expedition and the role of Inuit knowledge in the discoveries of the shipwrecks. # Polar bear safety

## Sirmilik National Park

### [Avoiding an encounter](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/sirmilik/securite-safety/ours-bears/eviter-avoid)

Essential safety tips and how to plan ahead to reduce the risk of encountering polar bears in Sirmilik.

### [Handling an encounter](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/sirmilik/securite-safety/ours-bears/rencontre-encounter)

What to do if your group encounters a polar bear in Sirmilik, how to prepare, and how to get help in an emergency.

### [Choosing a safe campsite](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/sirmilik/securite-safety/ours-bears/camping)

Where to set up your tent, places to avoid, and best practices to prevent polar bears from approaching your camp in Sirmilik.

### [Deterrents and warning systems](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/sirmilik/securite-safety/ours-bears/dispositifs-deterrents)

Bear spray, noisemakers, electric fences and other polar bear deterrents to keep your group safe in Sirmilik.

Nanuq, the great white bear, is found in many of Canada’s northern national parks and in some national historic sites. Whenever bears and people occupy the same area, conflict can arise. Polar bears and people have coexisted for thousands of years but contact between the two must be minimised to continue this legacy. Successful polar bear conservation requires your co-operation.

In Sirmilik National Park, polar bears are most active along the coast of the Borden Peninsula and along the north, west, and east coasts of Bylot Island. Be particularly cautious in March/April when females with cubs are emerging from their dens, and from July to October when the sea ice is gone and the bears are forced ashore. Polar bears may be encountered at other times of the year and in other areas of the park, even on glaciers. Always avoid camping near places where food may be cached or where harvesting activities (especially seal) have occurred, as polar bears may be attracted to these areas.

Each encounter with a polar bear is unique. Good judgement, common sense, and familiarity with polar bear behaviour are required in all situations. This information provides guidelines for avoiding and dealing with polar bear encounters. For your safety and the safety of the bears, please read this section carefully and seriously consider the risks involved with travel in polar bear country.

If you choose to travel in polar bear country, take the necessary precautions. The more people in your group, the greater the chances of deterring a bear. Read the following pamphlet carefully:

- [Safety in Polar Bear Country Pamphlet](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/nu/auyuittuq/archive/pdf/shared/PolarBearSafety_English.pdf) (PDF, 2.02 MB)

# Safety and guidelines

## Sirmilik National Park

Sirmilik offers spectacular scenery, wildlife, and opportunities to experience Inuit culture and learn about northern places. But there are a host of dangers associated with travel in this northern wilderness. The remoteness of this area and limited rescue capabilities increase the risk of the challenging natural hazards. All visitors must be prepared to deal with extreme and rapidly changing weather, unpredictable river crossings, high winds, and travel in polar bear country. You must be self-reliant and responsible for your own safety.

### [Important bulletins](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/sirmilik/securite-safety/bulletins)

Area closures, restricted activities and other important information that may affect visitors to Sirmilik National Park.

### [Visitor guidelines](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/sirmilik/securite-safety/comportements-guidelines)

Sirmilik National Park regulations, prohibited activities, registration information, environmental conservation practices and more.

### [Emergencies and rescue capability](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/sirmilik/securite-safety/urgence-emergency)

Emergency services, search and rescue, and how to prepare for medical, wildlife and weather-related emergencies in Sirmilik.

### [Communications](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/sirmilik/securite-safety/communication)

Connect to emergency services from Sirmilik using a satellite phone, InReach device or personal locator beacon.

### [Camping safety](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/sirmilik/securite-safety/camping)

What equipment to bring, how to choose a safe campsite, and food management tips for safe camping in Sirmilik.

### [Terrain hazards](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/sirmilik/securite-safety/terrestre-land)

How to avoid and prepare for rockfall, avalanches, glaciers and other terrain hazards in Sirmilik National Park.

### [Boat and kayak safety](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/sirmilik/securite-safety/plaisance-boating)

Find out what skills and equipment you need to travel safely in Sirmilik National Park by boat or sea kayak.

### [Polar bear safety](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/sirmilik/securite-safety/ours-bears)

How to avoid and manage polar bear encounters in Sirmilik, where to camp, and information on deterrents and warning systems.

### [Wildlife safety](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/sirmilik/securite-safety/faune-wildlife)

Safety tips to avoid and manage encounters with polar bears, foxes, wolves, and other wildlife in Sirmilik National Park.

### [River crossings](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/sirmilik/securite-safety/marine)

River crossings in Sirmilik can be dangerous. Pack the right gear, plan ahead and follow safe crossing techniques.

### [Snowmobile and qamutik safety](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/sirmilik/securite-safety/motoneige-snowmobile)

Snowmobile and qamutik travel across snow and ice can be dangerous. Learn how to avoid accidents and injuries.

### [Travel](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/sirmilik/securite-safety/voyage-travel)

Important information on emergency medical travel in Nunavut and travelling to Sirmilik with dangerous goods.

### [Weather, hypothermia and frostbite](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/sirmilik/securite-safety/meteo-weather)

Protect yourself in Sirmilik’s arctic climate. Bring the right equipment and be prepared for hazardous weather conditions.

Safety is everyone's responsibility. At Parks Canada, we do our part to make sure you can have a safe visit by assessing the risks, managing hazards, and making sure that safety information is freely available to everyone. You can do your part as visitors by making sure you seek out the information you need to stay safe and make well-informed decisions while enjoying these special places. Visit our websites and stop at a visitor center to speak with our employees for the most up to date information. Make sure you are fully prepared for whatever activities you choose to participate in so you can have a safe, enjoyable, and memorable visit.

For general information on how to stay safe and a list of the 10 essential items you should bring when enjoying the outdoors visit [**adventuresmart.ca**](http://www.adventuresmart.ca./)
